body:
Hello @robksawyer,

Looking at the [SPDX license inclusion principles](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/blob/main/DOCS/license-inclusion-principles.md), specifically other factors 1 and 3:

* In my view, this would not substantially comply with the open source and related definitions in "other factor" 1. As just one example, section 8.1 appears intended to mandate that certain users contribute money and/or code contributions back to the licensor, which would not be conformant to open source principles.
* For "other factor" 3, this license shows no evidence of actual, substantial use. The example projects given appear to be your own personal projects. Looking on GitHub I see some other references to "common sense license" texts, but they appear to be entirely different and unrelated licenses.

Given the above, I am marking this as not accepted and closing the issue.

Just to clarify though: You mentioned that "CSL is submitted as a LicenseRef". Please note that `LicenseRef-` identifiers are used for user-defined licenses that are _not_ on the [SPDX License List](https://spdx.org/licenses). You and anyone else are free to define and use license identifiers that start with the `LicenseRef-` prefix for your own local tagging and SBOMs, pursuant to the [SPDX specifications](https://spdx.dev/use/specifications/). See https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/annexes/spdx-license-expressions/ for more details.
